speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you're suffering from chronic left shoulder pain without a history of trauma. To help me understand what's going on, have you noticed if the pain is worse at night or if it's limited your ability to reach behind your back?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain disrupts your sleep and affects your daily activities like brushing your hair, yet you have no numbness or weakness in your arm. Given your age and 2-month history of worsening pain with movement, have you noticed a significant loss of range of motion, such as difficulty lifting your arm above your head?

REQUEST TEST: X_Ray_left_shoulder
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Radiographs (AP, Scapular Y, Axillary): Normal. No visible swelling or deformity noted on physical examination, though tenderness around the shoulder joint was present with restricted range of motion (Forward Flexion 75°, Abduction 75°, External Rotation 45°, Internal Rotation 15° with significant pain).

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray is normal, but your range of motion is severely restricted, particularly with internal rotation at only 15 degrees. Given your age, the chronic nature of the pain, and the specific limitation in internal rotation, do you notice that your hand cannot reach your lower back or the small of your waist?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray rules out fractures and dislocations, but your severe restriction in internal rotation (15 degrees) suggests the rotator cuff may no longer be functioning properly. I need to confirm if you have a "painful arc" when lifting your arm between 60 and 120 degrees, and whether you can actively lift your arm to your ear without assistance.

REQUEST TEST: MRI_left_shoulder

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Left Shoulder: The imaging reveals a full-thickness tear of the supraspinatus tendon with retraction of the tendon edge. There is associated high-grade partial thickness fraying of the infraspinatus tendon. Moderate subacromial bursitis is present, consistent with the patient's report of pain disrupting sleep and activities of daily living. No evidence of acute fracture or dislocation. The rotator cuff muscle shows mild fatty infiltration, suggesting chronicity of the pathology.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Full-thickness tear of the left supraspinatus tendon with associated infraspinatus fraying and secondary subacromial bursitis.
